page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top left, catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: ut, Spectatum veniunt, veniunt spectentur ut ipsæ, Ovid. Interdum verbum motus regit Græco more Infinitum: ut, inde venit judicare vivos & mortuos. Pro judicatum, seu ad judicandum, seu judicaturus, quæ postrema formula omnium est eruditissima.
Verbum motus e loco rexit olim supinum in u: ut, paterfamilias primus cubitu surgat, postremus cubitum eat, Cato. Obsonatu redeo, Plautus.
Verbum Infinitum regit ante se Accusativum, qui exponitur per Quod vel Ut, post se autem casum sui verbi: ut, Meum natum rumor est amare Terentius. Id est, Rumor est quod meus natus amet.

Post verba, Loco, ich verdinge[?]/conduco, ich dinge/bestelle/mando, ich befehle/curo, ich verschaffe/ich lasse/habeo, ich muß/& si qua sunt alia, non ponitur Accusativus cum infinito, sed Adjectivum participiale in dus, quod cum substantivo convenit: ut, loco faciendam sepulturam. Conduxit columnam faciendam. Gladiatores vi rapiendos, reservandosque mandabat. Curavit jaciendos lapides. Habeo eos consolandos. Hæc ex Vallæ elegantiar. lib.1.cap.27.

Interest, es ist daran gelegē / & refert, es gehet an/ regunt Genitivum, & hosce Ablativos, mea, tua, sua, nostra, vestra & cuja: ut, interest omnium recte facere, Cicero Reipublicæ refert confervari literas. Tua quod nihil refert, percontari desinas, Terentius. Non Tui. Permagni nostra refert. Non Nostri.

Miseret, es jammert mich / miserescit, es erbarmet mich / tædet, es verdreust mich / piget, es verdreust mich / pœnitet, es reuet mich / pudet, ich schäme mich. regunt Accusativum, cum Genitivo vel Infinito: ut,

page.notes: The scan is a fold-in-the-gutter photo with uneven lighting; the text is clear throughout. The German glosses are in black letter and are marked with bl. "verdinge" in the first gloss line is a doubtful reading (marked [?]). The running head is set in small capitals and transcribed as GRAMMATICA. The rule headings are numbered canons set in italic and are kept as paragraphs, not headings. The catchword "Nonne" is at bottom right. Some German words in the marginal-style glosses sit inline, and their exact slash and spacing follow the scan.
